- Then edx becomes encoded[i] for the next iteration

# Encoded data at 0x402060
encoded = bytes([0x79, 0xc5, 0x06, 0x4d, 0xc8, 0x2c, 0x5f, 0x93, 0xf7, 0x56, 0xb8, 0x2a, 0x5e, 0xcc, 0x2f, 0x97, 0xf6, 0x5a, 0x8d, 0xf0, 0x20, 0x99, 0x16])

# Starting value of dl (edx's low byte)
dl = 0x33

# The algorithm:
# For each i:
#   dl = (dl + input[i]) & 0xFF
#   Compare dl to encoded[i]
# So: input[i] = (encoded[i] - previous_dl) & 0xFF
# After comparison, dl becomes encoded[i] for next iteration

result = []
for i in range(23):
    # input[i] = (encoded[i] - dl) & 0xFF
    char_val = (encoded[i] - dl) & 0xFF
    result.append(char_val)
    # After adding input[i] to dl, dl becomes encoded[i]
    dl = encoded[i]

decoded = bytes(result)
print("Decoded:", decoded)
print("As string:", decoded.decode('ascii', errors='replace'))
